roadmaps.title: Top-5% in 35 engineering domains
roadmaps.description:
Top 5% in all of: Computer science, Data structures and algorithms, Maths, Probability, Statistics, C and C++, Operating systems, Linux, Bash, Network, Python, Java, Rust, Databases, Database administration, Data-intensive systems, Kafka and streaming, Spark and batch processing, Data engineering, DataOps, Data analysis, Data science, Machine learning, Deep learning, MLOps, Software engineering, System design, API design, Web development, Docker and Podman, Kubernetes, DevOps, Cloud, Cybersecurity, DevSecOps.

18 phases, about 4,840 hours at 22 hours a week, from 2026-10-19 (a Monday) to 2031-01-05. Each phase has a project that builds on the previous one, and each domain has a certification (43 in all) and project work that proves it. The skills assessment is retaken at every phase's end. 22–26 hours a week, 200 € a month (books, a cloud sandbox, a certification fund, a reward fund).

Weekly rhythm: Monday theory, Tuesday the core track, Wednesday practice, Thursday whichever is behind, Friday spaced tests and 3 DSA problems, Saturday 4 h project + 2 h DSA + 1 h notes, Sunday 3 h project + 2 h reading + 1 h Zettel + the weekly reflection.

- [ ] C and C++: C++ Institute CPP certification, CS:APP labs, all BusTub projects, sqlc-cpp clang-tidy clean.

- [ ] Database administration: EDB PostgreSQL Associate then Professional; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Cassandra runbooks with recorded failover and restore drills.

habits.title: Daily study block
habits.stack: After dinner on weekdays; at 09:00 on weekends
habits.cue: At the desk, the phone in another room.
habits.craving: Small daily compounding beats heroic weekends.
habits.two: Open today's first task and do one 25-minute pomodoro: a day counts after 25 focused minutes.
habits.reward: Tick the day and watch the streak grow; +1 rest token every 6 study days (bank up to 4), and streak rewards from the 20 € fund.
habits.identity: I'm someone who studies every day.

habits.title: Daily review: spaced tests and the board
habits.stack: When I sit down for the study block, before new material
habits.craving: Retrieval and spacing make 2.5 years of material stick; without them, phase 1 is gone by phase 4.
habits.two: Answer the oldest due test, then move today's tasks to Doing (15 minutes at most).
habits.reward: A cleared board; new material only once the old is retrieved.

habits.title: Weekly project deep-work session
habits.cue: No notifications, the current phase project open.
habits.craving: Projects turn reading into skill and build the portfolio that proves the top 5%.
habits.two: Pick one project task and run the tests; aim for a 4-hour block that ends with a commit.
habits.reward: Push to GitHub and enjoy the green CI badge; a finished feature earns the afternoon off from theory.

habits.title: Weekly reflection and roadmap check
habits.stack: Sunday, the last hour of the weekend block
habits.craving: A 2.5-year plan only survives if it's re-planned every week.
habits.two: Hours done against 22, what I learned, what's stuck, the token bank, next week's 5–8 tasks. Last Sunday of the month: the roadmap check.

- Subjects: ALL_SCHOOL_42 (last updated 2022: check each subject's version)
- Newer subjects and testers: GitHub topics 42 (https://github.com/topics/42) and 42-cursus (https://github.com/topics/42-cursus)
- Exam practice: 42_examshell, ranks 02–06 (https://github.com/terminal-42s/42_examshell)
- A 42-like environment: 42-Devcontainer (https://github.com/opsec-infosec/42-Devcontainer)
- Python projects checker: Germinette (https://github.com/ExceptedPrism3/germinette)
- To compare after yours passes: mcombeau/42_cursus_projects (https://github.com/mcombeau/42_cursus_projects)
- Not covered by 42: Java, Rust, and database administration, which come from the phase resources.

resources.title: Certification exams
resources.description:
43 certifications over 220 weeks, paid from the certification fund. Listed prices add up to about $4,893; the others (and OSCP+, sold with its course) vary by region and bundle: check them when you book. Watch for Linux Foundation, Red Hat, and Cyber Monday discounts. If the fund runs short, the domain's proof without the exam still counts.
